text:
Alex: Anyone else seeing a spike in mTLS handshake failures from EU proxies since ~08:10 UTC? logs show 'client cert not recognized' and a bunch of KMS decrypt denies.
Maria: Yep, noticed it on the latency dashboard and alerting. KMS denies around 08:12 UTC.
Nora: I pushed a policy tweak to key-role yesterday to add an `aws:SourceVpc` condition for tighter scope — that should only affect the extractor role, not the proxy keystore.
Samir: If that condition landed globally on the keystore role somehow, inter-region proxies that route via NAT could fail decrypt. Quick question: are we sure the proxy uses the same role?
Alex: Proxy uses service/keystore role in each region. We have a cross-account trust path for EU -> us-east for fallback decrypts. If condition excludes that path, decrypts fail.
Maria: Snippet from proxy logs: 
```
2026-03-21T08:11:55Z proxy-xyz TLS handshake failed: unwrap error: KMS:AccessDeniedException: user arn:aws:sts::123456:assumed-role/proxy-keystore role/extractor denied by condition (SourceVpc)
```
Nora: Ugh. I did update the shared role policy but scoped to `role/extractor` — possible I referenced the wrong role ARN in the change. Rolling back now.
oncall-bot: Incident INC-2026-0123 created and assigned to eng-security.
Alex: Short-term options: 1) Roll policy change back (fast once approved). 2) Enable keystore cache fallback so existing keys are used for N minutes. 3) Route EU decrypts to a regional KMS key (longer). Which do we want?
Samir: Cache fallback is fastest if we can flip the flag safely; but note we intentionally disabled fallback for keystores on deny to prevent silent key misuse.
Maria: I think rollback + enable short cache window is safest: rollback should restore decrypts immediately and cache reduces blast if another bad change occurs.
Nora: Rolling back now — will push policy revert and post the change id here.
Alex: While Nora does that, can someone add better audit tags so a KMS deny surfaces more clearly? Right now CloudTrail shows Decrypt denied but lacks the request-level app tag. We need `x-rt-session` or similar propagated into KMS request context to map denies to service requests.
Samir: Agreed. We can add per-request `context` with `applicationId` and `sessionId` to the KMS decrypt call. That will appear in CloudTrail as `requestParameters` and ease triage. I'll draft the change.
Maria: Also update runbook step 2 to include this CloudTrail quick query to find denies in the last 15m:
```
fields @timestamp, eventName, awsRegion, userIdentity.arn, errorMessage
| filter eventName = "Decrypt" and errorMessage like /AccessDenied/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 50
```
Alex: Good. Add another runbook step to check the proxy's `keystore_cache_hits` metric and `kms_decrypt_denies` counter.
Nora: Revert submitted: change-id ch-2026-89, applied at 08:15 UTC. Post-deploy checks show decrypt success rate climbing.
Maria: Confirming handshakes recovering in EU — client cert recognition is back. Will monitor for 30m.
Samir: I'll open a PR to: (a) add request context tags on decrypt calls, (b) add a temporary safe cache fallback flag guarded by an operator switch, (c) instrument an alert that correlates KMS Deny spikes with handshake errors.
Alex: Also let's add an automated test that ensures policy conditions we add don't accidentally exclude cross-region service principals. Maybe a CI check that validates `aws:SourceVpc` conditions against known proxy egress paths.
Maria: Filing follow-up tasks: ENGSEC-3421 (postmortem + policy audit), INFRA-2110 (keystore cache feature), TOOLING-801 (CloudTrail queries in console).
Nora: Sorry team — my change was meant to reduce blast radius. Going to add a checklist for policy edits: (1) confirm roles impacted, (2) simulate CloudTrail denies via policy emulator, (3) notify eng-security channel.
Alex: Thanks. Quick aside — can we emit a distinct metric `kms_policy_change_applied{role=\"...\"}` on policy rollout? Then SRE/SEC can correlate policy deploys to deny spikes.
Samir: Yep. I'll add that to the rollout pipeline.
Maria: For the incident record: root cause = policy condition added to shared role that accidentally matched proxy keystore ARN; mitigation = revert change; follow-ups = instrumentation + CI guard + runbook updates.
Alex: Closing loop: monitor for 60m, then assign postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
